Hi! I'm not a programmer, but I'd love a little tool for keeping track of shared costs when I go on trips with friends, so at the end we know who owes whom. Could you make it for me here?

My friend Sam writes scripts and is going to help me hook it up to a spreadsheet, so he wrote down how it should work. He says it should run with the Python that's already on my Mac, without installing anything else, by typing `python3 -m kitty` and a command in this folder, and it should keep everything in a file called `kitty.json` in the folder I run it from.

Here are the commands Sam wrote down:

- `init EUR` starts a new kitty, with EUR (or whatever we're using) as the main currency.
- `member add NAME`, `member remove NAME`, and `member list` for who's in the group.
- `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION` for when someone pays for something. By default it's split equally between everyone, and it should print the expense's ID number. Extras: `--among A,B` to split it equally between only some people; `--exact A=30,B=20`, `--shares A=2,B=1`, or `--percent A=60,B=40` to split it unevenly; `--currency USD` if it was paid in another currency; `--date 2026-07-14` (otherwise it's today); and `--category food` (otherwise "other").
- `expense list` and `expense remove ID`.
- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT` for when someone pays someone else back, also with `--currency` and `--date`.
- `rate set USD 0.92` means one USD is worth 0.92 of the main currency.
- `balances` shows how far up or down each person is overall: positive if they're owed money, negative if they owe.
- `settle` suggests who should pay whom to even everything out.
- `history NAME` lists everything that affected one person, with their running total.
- `report` shows how much each person spent on each category, counting their share of each expense, not what they paid.
- `export FILE` saves the expenses to a CSV file (for the spreadsheet) with the columns id, date, payer, description, amount, currency, category, and base_amount.

Sam also said the reports should print in a format called JSON so his scripts can read them, with money written as text with two decimals, in the main currency unless it's an expense's own amount. His examples:

- `member list`: `["Alice", "Bob"]`
- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

And if I type something wrong, like a name that isn't in the group or an amount that isn't a number, it should tell me what's wrong and stop (Sam says with "exit status 1"), not crash.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

"""Command-line interface: `python3 -m kitty COMMAND ...`.

Reports are printed as JSON. Commands that only change the kitty print
nothing when they succeed, except `expense add`, which prints the new ID.
Any mistake prints "error: ..." and exits with status 1.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import sys

from . import core
from .core import KittyError, fmt


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """An argument parser that exits with status 1 on bad usage."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, "error: {}\n".format(message))


def output(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False))


# --------------------------------------------------------------- commands

def cmd_init(args):
    if os.path.exists(core.DATA_FILE):
        raise KittyError(
            "there's already a kitty in this folder ({}). Delete or move that "
            "file first if you really want to start over".format(core.DATA_FILE))
    core.save(core.new_kitty(core.parse_currency(args.currency)))


def cmd_member_add(args, data):
    data["members"].append(core.validate_new_name(data, args.name))
    return True


def cmd_member_remove(args, data):
    name = core.require_member(data, args.name)
    if core.is_involved(data, name):
        raise KittyError(
            "{} is part of expenses or payments already, so they can't be "
            "removed (remove those first)".format(name))
    data["members"].remove(name)
    return True


def cmd_member_list(args, data):
    output(data["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args, data):
    payer = core.require_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = core.parse_money(args.amount)
    currency = (core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency
                else data["currency"])
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("the description can't be empty")
    category = (args.category or core.DEFAULT_CATEGORY).strip()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("the category can't be empty")
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()

    base_cents = core.to_base_cents(data, amount, currency)
    shares = core.compute_shares(data, base_cents, amount, currency,
                                 among=args.among, exact=args.exact,
                                 shares=args.shares, percent=args.percent)

    expense_id = data["next_expense_id"]
    data["next_expense_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "date": day,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": "{:.2f}".format(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {name: fmt(c) for name, c in shares.items()},
        "seq": next_seq(data),
    })
    output(expense_id)
    return True


def public_expense(e):
    return {key: e[key] for key in ("id", "date", "payer", "description",
                                    "amount", "currency", "base_amount",
                                    "category", "shares")}


def cmd_expense_list(args, data):
    output([public_expense(e) for e in data["expenses"]])


def cmd_expense_remove(args, data):
    try:
        expense_id = int(args.id)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("expense ID must be a whole number, got '{}'".format(args.id))
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["id"] == expense_id:
            data["expenses"].remove(e)
            return True
    raise KittyError("there's no expense with ID {}".format(expense_id))


def cmd_payment_add(args, data):
    sender = core.require_member(data, args.sender)
    receiver = core.require_member(data, args.receiver)
    if sender == receiver:
        raise KittyError("someone can't pay themselves back")
    amount = core.parse_money(args.amount)
    currency = (core.parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency
                else data["currency"])
    day = core.parse_date(args.date) if args.date else core.today()
    base_cents = core.to_base_cents(data, amount, currency)

    payment_id = data["next_payment_id"]
    data["next_payment_id"] += 1
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": payment_id,
        "date": day,
        "from": sender,
        "to": receiver,
        "amount": "{:.2f}".format(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),
        "seq": next_seq(data),
    })
    return True


def cmd_rate_set(args, data):
    currency = core.parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        raise KittyError("{} is the main currency; its rate is always 1".format(currency))
    rate = core.parse_positive(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    return True


def cmd_balances(args, data):
    output({name: fmt(c) for name, c in core.balances(data).items()})


def cmd_settle(args, data):
    output(core.settle(data))


def cmd_history(args, data):
    output(core.history(data, core.require_member(data, args.name)))


def cmd_report(args, data):
    output(core.category_report(data))


EXPORT_COLUMNS = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount",
                  "currency", "category", "base_amount"]


def cmd_export(args, data):
    try:
        with open(args.file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(EXPORT_COLUMNS)
            for e in data["expenses"]:
                writer.writerow([e[col] for col in EXPORT_COLUMNS])
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError("couldn't write {}: {}".format(args.file, e.strerror or e))


def next_seq(data):
    """A counter that remembers the order things were entered in."""
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- parser

def build_parser():
    parser = Parser(prog="python3 -m kitty",
                    description="Keep track of shared costs and who owes whom.")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    commands.required = True

    p = commands.add_parser("init", help="start a new kitty in this folder")
    p.add_argument("currency", help="main currency, e.g. EUR")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_init, needs_data=False)

    member = commands.add_parser("member", help="add, remove or list people")
    member_cmds = member.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    member_cmds.required = True
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("add", help="add someone to the group")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_add)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove someone from the group")
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_remove)
    p = member_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list the group")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_member_list)

    expense = commands.add_parser("expense", help="add, list or remove expenses")
    expense_cmds = expense.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    expense_cmds.required = True
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record something someone paid for")
    p.add_argument("payer")
    p.add_argument("amount")
    p.add_argument("description", nargs="+")
    p.add_argument("--among", metavar="A,B",
                   help="split equally between only these people")
    p.add_argument("--exact", metavar="A=30,B=20", help="split by exact amounts")
    p.add_argument("--shares", metavar="A=2,B=1", help="split by shares")
    p.add_argument("--percent", metavar="A=60,B=40", help="split by percentages")
    p.add_argument("--currency", help="currency it was paid in")
    p.add_argument("--date", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", help="date (default: today)")
    p.add_argument("--category", help="category (default: other)")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_add)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("list", help="list all expenses")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_list)
    p = expense_cmds.add_parser("remove", help="remove an expense by ID")
    p.add_argument("id")
    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_expense_remove)

    payment = commands.add_parser("payment", help="record someone paying someone back")
    payment_cmds = payment.add_subparsers(dest="action", metavar="ACTION")
    payment_cmds.required = True
    p = payment_cmds.add_parser("add", help="record a payment")
    p.add_argument("sender", metavar="FROM")
    p.add_argument("receiver", metavar="TO")
    p.add_argument("amount")

"""End-to-end tests: run `python3 -m kitty` exactly the way a person would.

Run with:  python3 -m unittest discover tests
"""

import csv
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from datetime import date

PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


class KittyTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.dir)

    def run_kitty(self, *args):
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=PROJECT)
        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "kitty"] + list(args),
                              cwd=self.dir, env=env, capture_output=True,
                              text=True)

    def ok(self, *args):
        result = self.run_kitty(*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0,
                         "{} failed: {}".format(args, result.stderr))
        return json.loads(result.stdout) if result.stdout.strip() else None

    def fails(self, *args, message=""):
        before = self.read_file()
        result = self.run_kitty(*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stdout + result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error:", result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(message, result.stderr)
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(self.read_file(), before, "failed command changed the file")
        return result.stderr

    def read_file(self):
        path = os.path.join(self.dir, "kitty.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            return None
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()

    def group(self, *names, currency="EUR"):
        self.ok("init", currency)
        for name in names:
            self.ok("member", "add", name)


class SamsExamples(KittyTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.group("Alice", "Bob")
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Dinner",
                                 "--currency", "USD", "--date", "2026-07-14",
                                 "--category", "food"), 1)

    def test_member_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("member", "list"), ["Alice", "Bob"])

    def test_expense_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("expense", "list"), [{
            "id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice",
            "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD",
            "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
            "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}])

    def test_balances(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances"), {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"})

    def test_settle(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("settle"),
                         [{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}])

    def test_history(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("history", "Bob"), [{
            "date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner",
            "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}])

    def test_report(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("report"), {"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}})

    def test_export(self):
        self.ok("export", "trip.csv")
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "trip.csv"), newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            rows = list(csv.reader(f))
        self.assertEqual(rows, [
            ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency",
             "category", "base_amount"],
            ["1", "2026-07-14", "Alice", "Dinner", "45.00", "USD", "food", "41.40"]])


class Splitting(KittyTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.group("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")

    def shares_of(self, expense_id):
        for e in self.ok("expense", "list"):
            if e["id"] == expense_id:
                return e["shares"]

    def test_defaults(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "30", "Taxi")
        e = self.ok("expense", "list")[0]
        self.assertEqual(e["date"], date.today().isoformat())
        self.assertEqual(e["category"], "other")
        self.assertEqual(e["currency"], "EUR")
        self.assertEqual(e["shares"], {"Alice": "10.00", "Bob": "10.00", "Carol": "10.00"})

    def test_leftover_cents_are_not_lost(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "10", "Snacks")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Alice": "3.34", "Bob": "3.33", "Carol": "3.33"})
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances"),
                         {"Alice": "6.66", "Bob": "-3.33", "Carol": "-3.33"})

    def test_among(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "20", "Museum", "--among", "Bob,Carol")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Bob": "10.00", "Carol": "10.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances"),
                         {"Alice": "20.00", "Bob": "-10.00", "Carol": "-10.00"})

    def test_exact(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "Tickets", "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=20")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Alice": "30.00", "Bob": "20.00"})

    def test_exact_in_foreign_currency(self):
        self.ok("rate", "set", "USD", "0.92")
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "Tickets", "--currency", "usd",
                "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=20")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Alice": "27.60", "Bob": "18.40"})

    def test_shares(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "90", "Room", "--shares", "Alice=2,Bob=1")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Alice": "60.00", "Bob": "30.00"})

    def test_percent(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "45", "Boat", "--percent", "Alice=60,Bob=40")
        self.assertEqual(self.shares_of(1), {"Alice": "27.00", "Bob": "18.00"})

    def test_multiword_description(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Bob", "12.5", "Ice", "cream", "--category", "food")
        e = self.ok("expense", "list")[0]
        self.assertEqual((e["description"], e["amount"]), ("Ice cream", "12.50"))

    def test_split_mistakes(self):
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--exact", "Alice=30,Bob=10",
                   message="add up to 40.00")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--percent", "Alice=60,Bob=30",
                   message="must add up to 100")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--among", "Bob,Dave",
                   message="'Dave' is not in the group")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--among", "Bob,Bob",
                   message="twice")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--shares", "Alice=two",
                   message="must be a number")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--shares", "Alice",
                   message="NAME=VALUE")
        self.fails("expense", "add", "Alice", "50", "x", "--among", "Bob",
                   "--shares", "Bob=1", message="only one of")


class MoneyAndPayments(KittyTestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.group("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")

    def test_payment_evens_out(self):
        self.ok("expense", "add", "Alice", "30", "Taxi")
        self.ok("payment", "add", "Bob", "Alice", "10")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances"),
                         {"Alice": "10.00", "Bob": "0.00", "Carol": "-10.00"})
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("settle"),
                         [{"from": "Carol", "to": "Alice", "amount": "10.00"}])

    def test_payment_in_foreign_currency(self):
        self.ok("rate", "set", "GBP", "1.15")
        self.ok("payment", "add", "Bob", "Alice", "10", "--currency", "GBP")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("balances")["Bob"], "11.50")

    def test_settle_brings_everyone_to_zero(self):
        self.ok("member", "add", "Dan")
